title: Gemini
content:
## Overview

Google Gemini is a family of multimodal AI models that can be integrated into your Emergent applications for chat, content generation, vision tasks, and more. Emergent provides built-in support for Gemini models through the Universal LLM Key system, making it simple to add Google's latest AI capabilities to your app.

This guide walks you through setting up Gemini in your Emergent project and making your first API call.

---

## Prerequisites

Before you begin, you'll need:

- An active Emergent project
- A Google Cloud account with access to the Gemini API
- A Gemini API key from [Google AI Studio](https://makersuite.google.com/app/apikey) or Google Cloud Console

<Note>
Gemini API keys are free to generate, though usage may be subject to Google's rate limits and pricing based on your tier and model selection.
</Note>

---

## Getting Your Gemini API Key

<Steps>
<Step title="Navigate to Google AI Studio">
Visit [Google AI Studio](https://makersuite.google.com/app/apikey) and sign in with your Google account.
</Step>

<Step title="Create an API key">
Click **Get API key** or **Create API key**, then select an existing Google Cloud project or create a new one. Copy the generated key immediately—you won't be able to view it again.
</Step>

<Step title="Store the key securely">
Keep your API key in a secure location. You'll add it to Emergent in the next section.
</Step>
</Steps>

---

## Adding Gemini to Your Emergent Project

Emergent uses the [Universal LLM Key](/the-universal-llm-key) system to manage AI provider credentials securely. You can add your Gemini key either through the dashboard or by setting an environment variable.

### Option 1: Via the Emergent Dashboard

<Steps>
<Step title="Open your project settings">
Navigate to your project in the Emergent dashboard and open the **Settings** or **Integrations** tab.
</Step>

<Step title="Add the Gemini key">
Locate the **AI Providers** section, select **Google Gemini**, and paste your API key into the designated field.
</Step>

<Step title="Save your changes">
Click **Save** to securely store your key. Emergent encrypts all API keys at rest.
</Step>
</Steps>

### Option 2: Via Environment Variable

You can also provide your Gemini key as an environment variable in your project:

```bash
GOOGLE_API_KEY=your_gemini_api_key_here
```

<Tip>
Environment variables take precedence over dashboard settings, making them ideal for local development or CI/CD pipelines.
</Tip>

---

## Using Gemini in Your Code

Once configured, you can call Gemini models using standard AI SDK patterns or direct HTTP requests. Emergent automatically routes your requests through the Universal LLM Key system.

### Example: Chat Completion

<CodeGroup>
```javascript
// Using Vercel AI SDK
import { generateText } from 'ai';
import { google } from '@ai-sdk/google';

const result = await generateText({
  model: google('gemini-1.5-flash'),
  prompt: 'Explain how photosynthesis works in simple terms.',
});

console.log(result.text);
```

```python
# Using Google's Python SDK
import google.generativeai as genai

genai.configure(api_key=process.env.GOOGLE_API_KEY)
model = genai.GenerativeModel('gemini-1.5-flash')

response = model.generate_content(
    'Explain how photosynthesis works in simple terms.'
)
print(response.text)
```

```typescript
// Using fetch directly
const response = await fetch(
  'https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/models/gemini-1.5-flash:generateContent',
  {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: {
      'Content-Type': 'application/json',
      'x-goog-api-key': process.env.GOOGLE_API_KEY,
    },
    body: JSON.stringify({
      contents: [{
        parts: [{ text: 'Explain how photosynthesis works in simple terms.' }]
      }]
    })
  }
);

const data = await response.json();
console.log(data.candidates[0].content.parts[0].text);
```
</CodeGroup>

---

## Available Gemini Models

Google offers several Gemini model variants optimized for different use cases:

| Model | Best For | Context Window |
|-------|----------|----------------|
| `gemini-1.5-pro` | Complex reasoning, long-form content, multimodal tasks | Up to 2M tokens |
| `gemini-1.5-flash` | Fast, efficient responses for most use cases | Up to 1M tokens |
| `gemini-1.0-pro` | Stable production workloads, text-only tasks | 32K tokens |

<Info>
Model availability and capabilities may change. Check [Google's documentation](https://ai.google.dev/models/gemini) for the latest model options and specifications.
</Info>

---

## Multimodal Capabilities

Gemini models support text, image, audio, and video inputs, making them ideal for applications that need to process multiple content types.

### Example: Vision Task

```javascript
import { generateText } from 'ai';
import { google } from '@ai-sdk/google';

const result = await generateText({
  model: google('gemini-1.5-flash'),
  messages: [
    {
      role: 'user',
      content: [
        { type: 'text', text: 'What is in this image?' },
        { type: 'image', image: 'https://example.com/photo.jpg' }
      ]
    }
  ]
});

console.log(result.text);
```

---

## Best Practices

<AccordionGroup>
<Accordion title="How do I choose between Gemini models?">
Use `gemini-1.5-flash` for most applications—it's fast and cost-effective. Switch to `gemini-1.5-pro` when you need maximum reasoning depth, very long context windows, or complex multimodal tasks. Use `gemini-1.0-pro` only if you need a stable, text-only model for production workloads.
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="How are API keys secured in Emergent?">
All API keys entered through the dashboard are encrypted at rest and never exposed in client-side code. Emergent's backend handles authentication transparently, so your keys remain secure even in public repositories.
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Can I use different Gemini models in the same project?">
Yes. You can specify the model name in each API call, allowing you to mix `gemini-1.5-flash` for simple queries and `gemini-1.5-pro` for complex tasks within the same application.
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="What if I hit rate limits?">
Google enforces rate limits based on your API tier. If you encounter `429` errors, implement exponential backoff in your retry logic or upgrade your Google Cloud quota. Emergent does not impose additional rate limits on Gemini calls.
</Accordion>
</AccordionGroup>

---

## Troubleshooting

<Warning>
If you see authentication errors, verify that your `GOOGLE_API_KEY` is correctly set and that the key has not been revoked or restricted in the Google Cloud Console.
</Warning>

Common issues and solutions:

- **"API key not valid"** — Double-check that you copied the full key without extra spaces. Regenerate the key in Google AI Studio if needed.
- **"Model not found"** — Ensure you're using a valid model identifier (e.g., `gemini-1.5-flash`). Some models may require allowlist access.
- **Slow responses** — Gemini Pro models may take longer for complex requests. Consider using Flash models for latency-sensitive applications.
- **CORS errors** — Gemini API calls should be made server-side. If calling from the browser, proxy requests through your Emergent backend.
